title: Interference from a sprinkler near the green
question: If a sprinkler head by the green is only in your putting line but does not affect your stance or the area of your intended swing, what must you do?

choices.text: Take free relief and move your ball.
Play your ball as it lies.
Move your ball to the fringe without penalty.
Take a penalty and move your ball.

explanation: You only get free relief when the sprinkler interferes with your stance or your area of intended swing, not just your line of play.

juniorVersion.title: What to Do If a Sprinkler Is in Your Way Near the Green
juniorVersion.question: You are putting, and a sprinkler head is in the way of your ball rolling to the hole, but it is not where your feet stand or where you swing your club. What should you do?

choices.text: Move your ball for free and play from a new spot.
Play your ball from where it is.
Move your ball onto the short grass by the green with no penalty.
Take a penalty and move your ball.

juniorVersion.explanation: You only get to move your ball for free if the sprinkler is where your feet stand or where you swing. If it is just in the way of your putt, you play the ball as it is.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A small metal or plastic top on the ground that sprays water to water the grass.
The path your ball tries to roll on to get to the hole when you putt.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Show children where a sprinkler might be on the green and help them see if it is in the spot where they stand, swing, or just on their line. Practise deciding when moving is allowed.
likelyMisconceptions: Kids may think you can always move your ball if the sprinkler is in the way of the putt.
They might not know it matters where you stand or swing instead.
